steps.text: Sunday's turkey & okra stew — take the lot, 470/590 g (1,060 g total) of the ~1.05 kg batch: turkey (120/160 g), okra (120/150 g), passata (120/140 g), pepper (70/90 g), onion (40/50 g) and the oil (7/9 g) they were cooked in — into a pan on medium with a splash of water. 4 minutes, no more.
Spinach (100/130 g) in two handfuls, wilted through.
Sunday's rice (62/85 g dry) warmed alongside, covered, 2 minutes.
Lime or lemon at the table. Okra wants acid.

why: The okra was cooked briefly on Sunday and will not survive a second long heating. Four minutes to warm through — go longer and you get the slime everyone complains about instead of the body it is supposed to give the stew.
notes: PLAN §4 worst-offender fix: this batch lunch previously had no stated portion against Sunday's ~1.05 kg stew. batchTakeG now states the exact take (470/590 g), which matches the Sunday yield exactly (single consumer, zero headroom) — see prep-b.json's yields.headroomNote for the reconciliation (470+590=1,060, matching the op's own ingredient sum of 90+160+280+260+270).

D0-003: oil (7/9 g) is entirely a Sunday cooking use (sautéing the stew's onion and pepper before the mince, passata and okra go in) — renamed olive_oil -> rapeseed_oil, unchanged grams. It is folded into the batch take at step 1 rather than added fresh at reheat, since it was never a separate ingredient the reheat itself uses.
Two short parallel tracks (stew pan + rice pan warming 'alongside', per the original wording) rather than treating the rice as a strictly sequential afterthought.
freebies carry the Sunday op's own trace seasoning (thyme, stock powder, scotch bonnet) forward with the batch take, same logic as the oil; lime/lemon are this card's own table seasoning.
